transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-09
Start time: 13:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE); Dr. Priya Suri (Nimbus Head of AI); Carlos Mendes (Nimbus Infra); Aisha Rahman (Nimbus PM); Samir Gupta (Nimbus Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync to review onboarding progress, re-check access, and tune SLAs for the POC. Focus areas: staging benchmarks, KV cache behavior, VPC peering and firewall, SOC2/KMS questions, and next steps for canary.

Topics:
- Staging latency and batch tuning
- Access gating and VPC peering
- Security docs and KMS integration
- Canary criteria and rollback plan

Action items: see metadata list

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey team thanks for joining, looks like we have the usual crew, I'll hand to Liam for the bench recap but first quick roll call
[00:12] Dr. Priya: hi all, good to see. we had some infra meetings this morning so hoping to close the VPC questions today
[00:18] Carlos: yep, we're on the line for peering windows, got a note but need final ok from cloud ops
[00:25] Liam: ok quick recap—last week we ran the 1k sample with the default batching and saw p50 ~90ms p95 ~480ms on the staging cluster, CPU looked fine but the KV cache hit rate was only about 22% which is low for their prompt shapes
[00:44] Aisha: that KV number sounds lower than we expected, we sent a prompt set with long prefixes, was there truncation?
[00:50] Liam: there's some misalignment—our prefix capture expects consistent tokenization. staging used the newer tokenizer build so some prefixes missed, that explains hits. i'll re-run with the canonical tokenizer
[01:05] Carlos: can you also include memory profile? last run spiked GPU memory a bit and the autoscaler started prewarming extra nodes
[01:12] Liam: will include memory timeline and process-level logs. we also observed occasional 5xxs when the pool scaled quickly under burst. thinking about reducing max batch timeout so we don't hold requests too long
[01:28] Maya: quick question from procurement—is there any change to cost estimate if we do smaller batch timeout? customers will ask for cost delta
[01:35] Liam: smaller timeout usually lowers tail latency but hurts throughput efficiency, so costs per token may go up slightly maybe 5-15% depending on steady-state. we can run a short AB with different timeout values
[01:47] Dr. Priya: our priority is predictability for clinicians; p95 < 600ms is acceptable but jitter kills UX. cost is secondary but we need a clear number
[01:58] Maya: noted. we'll produce a cost/latency matrix after the AB runs
[02:04] Samir: pm for security here—i'm still missing SOC two artifacts and details on customer-managed KMS integration. we need to validate key rotation and audit logs
[02:14] Maya: apologies Samir, we prepared the packet but didn't send it—i'll attach SOC2 report, iso summary, and KMS integration notes by Thursday
[02:22] Samir: great. also can you confirm whether Redwood stores any plaintext data in their control plane? i need explicit statement
[02:30] Liam: standard behavior—no persistent plaintext of customer inputs in control plane. we store audit metadata and encrypted blobs; full details in the security doc. i'll flag the exact section in the packet
[02:40] Carlos: about VPC peering—our cloud ops needs CIDR and port ranges for the infra, is there a template
[02:47] Maya: yes we've got a peering template, i'll share; it includes ports for health, metrics, and the gateway. reminder that for private deployment we can also support a customer-hosted gateway
[02:58] Aisha: can you remind us of the difference between dedicated and private for this POC? we had mixed notes
[03:05] Liam: short version—dedicated means reserved GPU pools in Redwood region with isolation; private means we deploy control plane into your VPC or on-prem, so network traffic stays in your network and you manage keys. for regulated data private is recommended
[03:20] Aisha: ok makes sense

[03:30] Liam: back to benching—i'll run two AB variants: timeout 20ms and timeout 50ms with KV cache improved heuristics. 5k requests each, same prompt mix. plan to run on Thursday in the staging window
[03:46] Carlos: Thursday looks ok, but need to reserve nodes. can you give an ETA when you'll kick off
[03:51] Liam: Thursday 02:00 UTC is what i'm thinking, should take ~2 hours including logs
[03:57] Carlos: that's in our window, i'll schedule pre-warm
[04:02] Dr. Priya: also can you push a run with a slightly longer prefix capture? our prompts frequently have patient notes up to 800 tokens
[04:10] Liam: yes, i'll increase kv prefix window and also include a run with no prefix caching to see worst-case
[04:18] Maya: nice. about canary criteria—Aisha can you walk through what you want as success metrics
[04:24] Aisha: sure—p95 under 600ms, error rate under 0.5% on user queries, and semantic quality measured by our eval set (we need at least 94% pass on intent preservation). also cost per 1k responses under $X based on our budget, i'll send final number
[04:42] Maya: sounds reasonable. we'll map each metric to a rollback condition
[04:46] Samir: on rollback, need a plan for key revocation and audit trail, and a documented fallback to a non-sensitive path if we detect potential data exfil
[04:55] Liam: fallback is simple—route to a redwood-hosted safe model that strips PII and returns a template answer. we'll document routing rules

[05:10] Maya: any open risks from your side Carlos?
[05:14] Carlos: main risk is VPC peering scheduling and egress rules; another is our infra team wants exact outbound IPs for allowlist which requires confirmation
[05:25] Maya: we can give a short list of egress IPs for the peering window. not ideal long-term but fine for POC
[05:32] Dr. Priya: i wanted to flag a stakeholder—our CISO wants a short Security Q&A session with Redwood next week, Samir will coordinate
[05:40] Samir: yes, once i have the packet i'll schedule a 30-minute call
[05:45] Maya: great, i'll put a tentative invite and Samir can confirm

[06:00] Liam: small note on model variants—we tested the quantized variant yesterday, it saves cost but increased hallucination on a couple of medical prompts. i'd recommend using full-precision for clinical-critical flows
[06:18] Dr. Priya: good catch. can we do hybrid routing? critical endpoints to full-precision, bulk summary to quantized
[06:26] Liam: yep that's supported. we can set routing policy by endpoint with automatic fallback if the full-precision node is unavailable
[06:34] Aisha: for the POC, let's do hybrid: triage and final answers on full-precision, batch summaries on quantized. need to document the routing rules and expected cost delta
[06:48] Maya: i'll include a routing policy draft with estimated cost numbers

[06:55] Carlos: one last infra question—how does KV cache persist across scaled nodes? if a node is evicted do we lose prefix state leading to cold starts?
[07:05] Liam: there's no global KV persisted across nodes in current setup. we use local KV per serving replica; warmups and sticky routing mitigate misses. for guaranteed warm cache we can pin sessions to specific replicas but that reduces flexibility
[07:20] Carlos: hmmm ok we need a note on warm-up time for short sessions
[07:25] Liam: will include warm-up curve and suggested prewarm strategy

[07:32] Maya: ok time for quick recap and next steps
[07:36] Liam: I'll run AB bench (5k each) Thursday 02:00 UTC, include canonical tokenizer, memory profile, KV hits, and 2 timeout settings
[07:45] Maya: I'll send SOC2, ISO snippets, KMS/HSM playbook and the VPC peering template by Thursday EOD (11/12)
[07:55] Carlos: I'll confirm peering window and outbound IP allowlist by Wednesday 11/11
[08:01] Aisha: I'll finalize canary success criteria and cost target by Friday 11/13
[08:07] Samir: i'll review the security packet and propose a 30-min CISO session for next week

[08:15] Maya: any other questions or blockers?
[08:18] Dr. Priya: nothing for now, thanks everyone
[08:22] Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites and the packet
[08:26] Liam: thanks, talk soon
[08:30] End of recording

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and some words transcribed phonetically (e.g., "SOC two" for SOC2, "kv cache" sometimes lowercased). Some speaker attributions may be generic.
